record.title: The near-field conjecture for sharply 2-transitive groups
record.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a sharply $2$-transitive permutation group, meaning that it acts transitively and freely on ordered pairs of distinct points. A **near field** is a skew field that is distributive only from the left. **Near-field conjecture.** There exists a near field $N$ such that

$$
\Gamma=N^{\times}\ltimes N.
$$

This conjecture characterizes sharply $2$-transitive groups as the affine groups of near fields. It was confirmed for finite sharply $2$-transitive groups by H. Zassenhaus in 1936, and the paper proves it for the linear groups under the stated hypotheses.
record.source_name: Yair Glasner and Dennis D. Gulko, “Sharply 2-transitive linear groups”, arXiv:1208.2427 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1208.2427

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of August 2012). “The conjecture was confirmed by H. Zassenhaus for finite sharply $2$-transitive groups in a 1936 paper.”

record.title: The conjecture for binomials x^{q-2}+t x^{q^2-q-1}
record.statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power and let $t\in\Bbb F_q^*$. Define

$$
f(x)=x^{q-2}+t x^{q^2-q-1}.
$$

**The conjecture for binomials $x^{q-2}+t x^{q^2-q-1}$.** The polynomial $f$ is a permutation polynomial of $\Bbb F_{q^2}$ if and only if one of the following holds: (i) $t=1$ and $q\equiv 1\pmod 4$; (ii) $t=-3$ and $q\equiv\pm1\pmod{12}$; or (iii) $t=3$ and $q\equiv-1\pmod 6$. This conjecture arose from the preceding theorem and a computer search of the remaining cases, and it aims to classify the permutation behavior of this binomial over $\Bbb F_{q^2}$.
record.source_name: Neranga Fernando, Xiang-dong Hou and Stephen D. Lappano, “A New Approach to Permutation Polynomials over Finite Fields, II”, arXiv:1208.2942 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1208.2942

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2012).

record.title: Conjecture on the nonexistence of homogeneous rotation symmetric bent functions
record.statement: A Boolean function is **homogeneous** if all its monomials have the same degree, and **rotation symmetric** if it is invariant under cyclic permutations of its variables. A Boolean function is **bent** when it has maximal distance from the affine Boolean functions. The degree of a Boolean function is its algebraic degree. **Nonexistence conjecture.** There are no homogeneous rotation symmetric bent functions of degree $>2$. This conjecture was proposed after exhaustive searches found no homogeneous rotation symmetric bent functions of degrees $3$, $4$, or $5$ in $10$ variables. The paper presents results supporting it, but the conjecture remains open in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Xiyong Zhang and Guangpu Gao, “On the conjecture about the nonexistence of rotation symmetric bent functions”, arXiv:1303.2282 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.2282

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2013).

record.title: Godbole–Goyt–Herdan–Pudwell recurrence conjecture for ordered partitions with blocks of size 2
record.statement:
An **ordered partition** of $[2k]$ with $k$ blocks of size $2$ is counted by $op_{[2^k]}(123)$ when it avoids the permutation pattern $123$. **Godbole–Goyt–Herdan–Pudwell's recurrence conjecture.** For $k\geq0$,

$$
op_{[2^{k+2}]}(123)= \frac{329k^3+1215k^2+1426k+528}{2(k+2)(2k+5)(7k+5)}op_{[2^{k+1}]}(123)+\frac{3(k+1)(2k+1)(7k+12)}{(k+2)(2k+5)(7k+5)}op_{[2^k]}(123).
$$

This conjecture arose from computer-generated recurrence discovery using Zeilberger's Maple package $FindRec$ and gives a second-order linear recurrence for the enumeration of $123$-avoiding ordered partitions with all blocks of size $2$.
record.source_name: William Y. C. Chen, Alvin Y. L. Dai and Robin D. P. Zhou, “Ordered Partitions Avoiding a Permutation of Length 3”, arXiv:1304.3187 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.3187

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2013).

record.title: The 4-adjacent Gray code conjecture for descent sequences in co-RGC order
record.statement:
A **descent sequence** is a restricted growth sequence defined analogously to an ascent sequence. List the set of length-$n$ descent sequences in the order $\prec_c$.

**4-adjacent Gray code conjecture.** The resulting list is a $4$-adjacent Gray code.

This conjecture concerns whether the co-RGC order has the bounded-adjacency Gray code property for descent sequences. It was checked by computer for $n\leq 10$; no general proof or disproof is given here.
record.source_name: Ahmad Sabri and Vincent Vajnovszki, “Two Reflected Gray Code based orders on some restricted growth sequences”, arXiv:1306.5464 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.5464

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2013).

record.title: The uniform domination conjecture for Steiner triple systems
record.statement:
Let $STS(v)$ denote a Steiner triple system of order $v$, and let $gamma(D)$ be the domination number of its incidence graph.

**Uniform domination conjecture.** There exists a function $f:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow\mathbb{N}$ such that, if $D\in STS(v)$, then

$$
\gamma(D)=f(v).
$$

Equivalently, the domination number depends only on the order $v$, not on the structure of the Steiner triple system. The conjecture is verified for $v\leq 15$, but remains open in general.
record.source_name: Felix Goldberg, Deepak Rajendraprasad and Rogers Mathew, “Domination in designs”, arXiv:1405.3436 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.3436

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2014). “Finally, a number of open questions are proposed.”

record.title: Character range conjecture for Stanley sequences
record.statement:
For a regular Stanley sequence $S(A)$, let $\lambda(A)$ denote its character. The **range of the character function** is the set of values attained by $\lambda(A)$ over regular Stanley sequences. **Character range conjecture.** This range is exactly

$$
\{n\in\mathbb{Z}: n\ge 0\}\setminus\{1,3,5,9,11,15\}.
$$

The claim is based on computational evidence: the six excluded values were found impossible in the examined cases, while all other values up to $76$ were realized; the source notes that the asserted impossibility was not definitive because irregularity had not been ruled out for certain sequences.
record.source_name: David Rolnick, “On the classification of Stanley sequences”, arXiv:1408.1940 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1408.1940

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2014).

record.title: The q-analogue identity for rook placements and the Harer–Zagier formula
record.statement:
Let $Y(n,s)$ be the set of all Young diagrams with $n$ rows of lengths between $s$ and $n+s$. For a rook placement $C$ on a diagram $[?]$ in $Y(n,s)$, let $\operatorname{inv}(C)$ be the number of blank squares left after crossing out every square directly to the left of or above a rook, let $|\mu|$ denote the number of squares of $\mu$, and write $[m]_q$ for the $q$-integer, $[m]_q!!$ for the corresponding $q$-double factorial, and $\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{a}{b}_q$ for the $q$-binomial coefficient. **The q-analogue conjecture.** The following identity holds:

$$
\sum_{\mu \in Y(n,s)} \prod_{i=1}^{n}q^{\mu_i-i}[\mu_i-i+1]_q = \sum_{\mu \in Y(n,s)}\sum_{\substack{\operatorname{rook placements}\\ C \,\operatorname{on}\, \mu}}q^{\operatorname{inv}(C) + |\mu| - \binom{n+1}{2}}
$$

$$
=\sum_{k\geq 0} q^{n(s-k) + \binom{k}{2}}[2n-1]_q!!\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{s}{k}_q\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{n}{k}_q\prod_{i=1}^k(1 + q^{n+i}).
$$

This gives a $q$-analogue of the rook-placement expression for the Harer–Zagier formula; it was verified computationally up to $n=10$ and $s=5$, but no proof or general resolution is supplied in the source.
record.source_name: Max Wimberley, “Towards a q-analogue of the Harer-Zagier formula via rook placements”, arXiv:1412.3182 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.3182

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2014).

record.title: The Kneser graph Hamiltonicity conjecture
record.statement: For integers $n$ and $k$ with $k\geq 1$ and $n\geq 2k+1$, let the **Kneser graph** $K(n,k)$ be the graph whose vertices are the $k$-element subsets of $[n]:=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$, with an edge between two vertices exactly when the corresponding sets are disjoint. **Kneser graph Hamiltonicity conjecture.** For any $k\geq 1$ and $n\geq 2k+1$, except for $(n,k)=(5,2)$, the Kneser graph $K(n,k)$ has a Hamilton cycle. This is a classical Hamiltonicity problem for Kneser graphs; the source notes computational confirmation for $n\leq 27$ and a best-known general result, but the full assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Torsten Mütze and Pascal Su, “Bipartite Kneser graphs are Hamiltonian”, arXiv:1503.09175 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.09175

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2015).

record.title: Prime-set determination conjecture for complete bipartite graphs
record.statement: Let $K_{n,n}$ be the complete bipartite graph with two partite sets of $n$ vertices. A **minimal coprime labeling** assigns distinct labels from $\{1,2,\ldots,k\}$ to its vertices, with adjacent labels relatively prime, where $k=\operatorname{\mathfrak{pr}}(K_{n,n})$ is minimal. **Prime-set determination conjecture.** For $K_{n,n}$, there exists a set of prime numbers $\{p_1,\ldots,p_j\}$ such that this set determines the values in the label sets of the two partite sets, giving $K_{n,n}$ a minimal coprime labeling. The source reports this pattern from computational analysis for $n\leq 13$; its general validity is presented as a conjectural observation and remains open.
record.source_name: Adam H. Berliner, Nathaniel Dean, Jonelle Hook, Alison Marr, Aba Mbirika and Cayla D. McBee, “Coprime and prime labelings of graphs”, arXiv:1604.07698 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.07698

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2016).

record.title: Carpenter–Tonchev rank conjecture for designs from maximal arcs
record.statement:
Let $t\geq 2$, and let $\mathcal{D}$ be a $2-(2^{2t-1}-2^{t-1},2^{t-1},1)$ design with incidence matrix $A$. **Carpenter–Tonchev's rank conjecture.** The binary rank of $A$ satisfies

$$
\operatorname{rank}_{2}(A)\geq 3^t-2^t,
$$

and equality

$$
\operatorname{rank}_{2}(A)=3^t-2^t
$$

holds if and only if $\mathcal{D}$ is embeddable as a maximal $(2^{2t-1}-2^{t-1},2^{t-1})$-arc in $PG(2^t,2)$. This strengthens a conjecture attributed to Laurel Carpenter that the binary rank of every design associated with a hyperoval in $PG(2,2^t)$ equals $3^t-2^t$, and generalizes a conjecture of A. E. Brouwer. The computations in the paper support the conjecture for the 93 designs arising from hyperovals in $PG(2,16)$, but the general assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Vladimir D. Tonchev and Tim Wagner, “Maximal (120,8)-arcs in projective planes of order 16 and related designs”, arXiv:1702.06909 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.06909

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).

record.title: The EW-tableaux Eulerian distribution conjecture
record.statement:
An **EW-tableau** is a tableau of the type considered in the paper, and $n$-permutations are permutations of $[n]$. Let $k$ be the number of columns containing a $0$, and let $A(n,k)$ denote the Eulerian number counting $n$-permutations with $k$ excedances.

**EW-tableaux Eulerian distribution conjecture.** The number of EW-tableaux of size $n$ with $k$ columns containing a $0$ equals

$$
A(n,k),
$$

the number of $n$-permutations with $k$ excedances.

The conjecture concerns an apparently Eulerian distribution on EW-tableaux. The authors state that they had not proved it and had verified it for $n\le 12$; no resolution is supplied in the given text.
record.source_name: Thomas Selig, Jason P. Smith and Einar Steingrimsson, “EW-tableaux, Le-tableaux, tree-like tableaux and the Abelian sandpile model”, arXiv:1711.01622 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.01622

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2017).

record.title: Rob Pratt's generating-function conjecture for the packing number of the double vertex graph of a path
record.statement:
Let $A085680(n)$ denote the packing number of the double vertex graph of the path graph $P_n$, equivalently $\rho(F_2(P_n))$, where $F_2(P_n)$ is the 2-token graph of $P_n$. Rob Pratt's conjecture asserts

$$
\sum_{n\geq 0} A085680(n+2)x^n=\frac{1-x+x^2-x^{10}+x^{11}}{(1-x)^2(1-x^5)}.
$$

This conjecture gives the ordinary generating function for the sequence whose exact values were known up to $n=50$ at the time it was posed; the supplied source does not indicate whether the conjecture has since been resolved.
record.source_name: José Manuel Gómez Soto, Jesús Leaños, Luis Manuel Ríos-Castro and Luis Manuel Rivera, “The packing number of the double vertex graph of the path graph”, arXiv:1711.03682 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.03682

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2017).

record.title: Nonexistence conjecture for regular 3-hypertopes with power-of-two automorphism groups
record.statement:
Let $n,s,t,l$ be positive integers satisfying

$$
n\geq 10,\qquad s,t\geq 2,\qquad l\geq 1,\qquad n<s+t+l.
$$
 A regular $3$-hypertope has **type** $(2^s,2^t,2^l)$ when its corresponding type parameters are $(2^s,2^t,2^l)$.

**Nonexistence conjecture.** There is no regular $3$-hypertope of type $(2^s,2^t,2^l)$ whose automorphism group has order $2^n$.

This conjecture proposes a restriction on the possible orders of automorphism groups of regular $3$-hypertopes with the specified power-of-two type. The paper establishes existence in related parameter ranges, while the asserted nonexistence for the stated inequalities remains unresolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Dong-Dong Hou, Yan-Quan Feng and Dimitri Leemans, “Existence of regular 3-hypertopes with 2^n chambers”, arXiv:1901.09034 (2019).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2019). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1901.07135](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.07135).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.09034

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2019).

record.title: Gallai-Ramsey number conjecture for the three-triangle fan
record.statement:
Let $F_n$ be the fan graph with $n$ triangles, defined by

$$
F_n=K_1+n\overline{K_2},
$$

so that $F_3$ is the fan with three triangles, and let $gr_k(K_3;F_3)$ denote the $k$-color Gallai-Ramsey number of $F_3$ versus $K_3$. **The authors' conjecture.** For $k\geq 2$,

$$
gr_k(K_3;F_3)=\begin{cases}
14\cdot 5^{\frac{k-2}{2}}-1, & \text{if }k\text{ is even};\\
33\cdot 5^{\frac{k-3}{2}}, & \text{if }k\text{ is odd}.
\end{cases}
$$

This asserts that the lower bound in the odd-$k$ case of the preceding theorem is sharp, completing the exact determination of the Gallai-Ramsey numbers for $F_3$. The even-$k$ case and the odd cases $k=3,5$ are proved in the paper, while the general odd case is left open.
record.source_name: Yaping Mao, Zhao Wang, Colton Magnant and Ingo Schiermeyer, “Gallai-Ramsey numbers for fans”, arXiv:1902.10706 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.10706

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2019).

record.title: The flow conjecture for 3-edge-connected cubic graphs excluding the Petersen graph
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a 3-edge-connected cubic graph different from the Petersen graph $P_{10}$. A **nowhere-zero $\mathbb{Z}_2^3$-flow** is a flow $f:E(G)\to\mathbb{Z}_2^3\setminus\{0\}$ satisfying flow conservation at every vertex. **Flow conjecture for 3-edge-connected cubic graphs excluding $P_{10}$.** There exist $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{Z}_2^3$ such that

$$
f^{-1}(\{\alpha,\beta\})
$$

is a matching in $G$, and there is no edge $e=uv$ of $G$ for which $u$ is incident to an edge $e_u$ and $v$ is incident to an edge $e_v$ satisfying $f(e_u)=\alpha$ and $f(e_v)=\beta$. If true, this would provide the flow-based route proposed in the paper toward the normal 6-edge-coloring conjecture. No resolution is supplied here.
record.source_name: Giuseppe Mazzuoccolo and Vahan Mkrtchyan, “Normal 6-edge-colorings of some bridgeless cubic graphs”, arXiv:1903.06043 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.06043

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of March 2019). “More precisely, he showed that a bridgeless cubic graph is a counterexample to this conjecture, if and only if, it does not admit a normal edge-coloring (see Definitions and in Section ) with at most $5$ colors.”

record.title: Flagged Grothendieck characterization conjecture for Lascoux polynomials
record.statement: Let $lambda$ be any partition and let $w\in S_n^{\lambda}$. A flagged Grothendieck polynomial is understood in the sense used in the paper, and $w$ is **312-avoiding** when it has no subsequence with relative order $312$. **Flagged Grothendieck characterization conjecture.** The Lascoux polynomial $L_{w\lambda}(\mathbf{x};\beta)$ is a flagged Grothendieck polynomial if and only if $w$ is 312-avoiding. This is the K-theoretic analogue of the corresponding characterization for Demazure characters at $beta=0$; the conjecture seeks to identify exactly which Lascoux polynomials admit flagged Grothendieck descriptions.
record.source_name: Oliver Pechenik and Travis Scrimshaw, “K-theoretic crystals for set-valued tableaux of rectangular shapes”, arXiv:1904.09674 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.09674

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2019).

record.title: Cyclic reciprocal squared-difference conjecture for permutations
record.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $\pi\in\mathfrak{S}_n$ be a permutation of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. **Cyclic squared-difference conjecture.** If $n>11$, there is a permutation $\pi$ such that

$$
\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}\frac{1}{\pi(k)^2-\pi(k+1)^2}+\frac{1}{\pi(n)^2-\pi(1)^2}=0.
$$

The paper introduces this as a further conjecture motivated by the preceding non-cyclic squared-difference conjecture, and explicitly distinguishes it from the conjectures of Sun it has just reproduced.
record.source_name: Guo-Niu Han, “On the existence of permutations conditioned by certain rational functions”, arXiv:1910.02662 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.02662

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2019).

record.title: Brualdi–Stein conjecture on near transversals in Latin squares
record.statement:
A **Latin square** is an $n\times n$ array in which each symbol occurs exactly once in every row and column. A **near transversal** is a partial transversal of length $n-1$, meaning a set of $n-1$ entries chosen from distinct rows and columns with distinct symbols.

**Brualdi–Stein conjecture.** Every Latin square contains a near transversal.

This conjecture is attributed to Brualdi and Stein, and in another source to Ryser. It has been proved for Cayley tables of finite groups and for Latin squares of order at most $11$, but remains open in general.
record.source_name: Darcy Best, Kyle Pula and Ian M. Wanless, “Small Latin arrays have a near transversal”, arXiv:1911.05936 (2021).
record.references:
**7 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012–2019). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1808.05213](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05213), [arXiv:1609.06346](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.06346), [arXiv:1510.02521](https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.02521), [arXiv:1504.05373](https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.05373), [arXiv:1503.00438](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.00438), [arXiv:1211.1306](https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.1306).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.05936

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2019). “Unfortunately, all but one of these conjectures has been disproven (only number (4) remains open).”

record.title: The Ramanujan–Kolberg identity conjecture for multipartitions
record.statement:
Let $p_t(n)$ denote the number of $t$-multipartitions of $n$. Let $a$ and $t$ be odd integers, with $3\mid t$ whenever $3\mid a$. Define $b$ by

$$
b\equiv \frac{t}{3}\cdot 8^{-1}
$$

when $3\mid t$, and by $b\equiv24^{-1}\pmod a$ otherwise, and set

$$
k=\left\lceil\frac{t(a^2-1)}{24a}\right\rceil.
$$

Here $f_d$ denotes the standard eta-product factor used in the source, and $\epsilon^t_{a,d,j}$ are coefficients in $\{0,1\}$. **Ramanujan–Kolberg identity conjecture.** There is a suitable choice of the $\epsilon^t_{a,d,j}$ such that $\epsilon^t_{a,1,0}=1$, $\epsilon^t_{a,d,j}=0$ whenever $at/d-24j<0$, and

$$
q^k\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}p_t(an+b)q^n\equiv\sum_{d\mid a}\sum_{j=0}^{\lfloor k/d\rfloor}\frac{\epsilon^t_{a,d,j}q^{dj}}{f_d^{at/d-24j}}.
$$

The conjecture predicts that these subprogression generating functions lie in a particularly structured, relatively low-dimensional space of modular forms. The supplied text says Chen proved it for, among other cases, all primes $a\geq3$, so the general conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: William J. Keith and Fabrizio Zanello, “Parity of the coefficients of certain eta-quotients, II: The case of even-regular partitions”, arXiv:2302.00708 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.00708

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2023).
